title: Three-Horizon Roadmap + Ops Runbook for Hosted API & Model Lineup
creator: Evan Chu
description:
Purpose:
This ticket captures a three-horizon roadmap approach and an operational runbook for the Hosted API model lineup. The goal is to provide the PM/Eng/Design teams with a single source of truth that ties quarterly commitments (Horizon 1) to near-term experimentation (Horizon 2) and longer-term platform investments (Horizon 3). The runbook portion codifies rollout gates, canary cadence, rollback criteria, and monitoring dashboards for model swaps and catalog additions.

Scope:
- Hosted API model catalog (curation, rotation, deprecation)
- Canary and phased rollout playbooks for model swaps (small->regional->global)
- Operational runbook: metrics, alerts, and escalation paths for model regressions (quality, latency, cost)
- Cross-functional cadences: roadmap syncs, risk reviews, and postmortems
- Alignment with Dedicated/Private release windows (minimal coupling required)

Deliverables (by horizon):
Horizon 1 (next 1 quarter):
- Committed hosted-model lineup for Q2 with canary schedules and owners.
- Ops runbook v1: rollback triggers (latency >1.8x baseline or NPS regressions), immediate mitigation steps, and contact matrix.
- Dashboards: per-model latency/cost/quality SLO panel and a model health index.

Horizon 2 (1–2 quarters):
- Controlled A/B experiment templates for lightweight model variants and quantization profiles.
- Model prioritization matrix (traffic, revenue sensitivity, regulatory footprint).
- Autoscaling and batch-policy experiments tied to real workloads.

Horizon 3 (3+ quarters):
- Policy-driven routing: automatic fallback rules across model variants and regions.
- Integrations with Dedicated scheduling policies so enterprise customers can opt into lineup changes.
- Incubation plan for a model QA lab (automated evals + synthetic user prompts).

Acceptance criteria:
- Roadmap doc approved by Eng, Design, and Security stakeholders.
- Ops runbook published in Confluence and linked in Console runbooks.
- Canary schedule tested in staging with one successful model swap (no customer-impacting regressions and automated rollback exercised).
- Health dashboards populated and able to trigger a PagerDuty alert for breach scenarios.

Rollout and gating rules (ops runbook highlights):
- Canary stage: 0.5% traffic for 24h in a single region; guardrails: latency P95 <= 1.4x baseline, error rate delta <= 0.05pp, user-facing quality metric within guardrail set.
- Regional ramp: 5% for 48h across 2 regions if canary passes.
- Global ramp: incremental 25% steps per 24h with continuous monitoring; automatic rollback if any guardian metric exceeds threshold for 30m window.
- Manual hold: PM or SRE can pause rollout at any gate.

Monitoring & SLOs to enforce:
- Latency: P95 per-model per-region (goal <= 350ms for small models, <= 700ms for larger LLMs used in hosted tiers).
- Token cost delta: expected unit cost within +/−10% of projection during rollout.
- Quality regression: prompt-set evals aggregated into a model health score; automatic rollback at >6-point drop.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Sudden cost spike from workload mismatch. Mitigation: temporary throttling to existing model and alert to cost ops.
- Risk: Model produces unsafe outputs in a narrow distribution. Mitigation: immediate traffic quarantine for the offending cohort and fast-track evaluation.
- Risk: Enterprise OpenSCAP or compliance mismatch. Mitigation: tie any lineup changes to a compliance checklist and require security sign-off for Private/Dedicated-affecting moves.

2) SRE to create necessary alerting queries and routing rules for the canary pipeline (due 2026-03-30).
3) Runbook review with Security (due 2026-04-07).
